system.context: Orbit fine-tuned its assistant on support chats; the training loss fell and the model learned to repeat the customer's question before answering. The trainer computed the loss on every token of every row, prompt included, so a third of what the model was rewarded for predicting was the customer's side of the conversation.
system.request: A worked Python example of one action: build_labels(example, vocab) and pad_batch(rows). The first encodes the prompt and the completion with a stand-in tokenizer that gives each new word the next id (0 and 1 reserved for pad and eos), builds the input ids as prompt plus completion plus eos, and builds labels of the same length with -100 over every prompt position and the completion ids and eos over the rest, raising ValueError for an empty completion. The second pads every row on the right to the longest with the pad id, -100 labels, and an attention mask. The lesson leads with the complete solution and its exact output over three inline examples (each row's ids and labels, the padded batch with masks, the trained count of 20 of 33, the rejected empty completion), explains the Python construct by construct, traces every row, and offers one practice variation: fitting rows into a maximum length by dropping prompt tokens from the left.
inputs: Three examples written inline in solution.py as dictionaries with a prompt and a completion: 'how do i reset my password' / 'use the forgot password link', 'where is my invoice' / 'open billing and choose invoices', 'cancel my plan' / 'go to billing and choose cancel plan'; PAD 0, EOS 1, IGNORE -100
outputs: Rows of 12, 10, and 11 positions whose labels are -100 over 6, 4, and 3 prompt positions and the completion ids plus eos over the rest; a batch padded to 12 with masks; 20 trained tokens of 33 real tokens (61 percent)

python solution.py prints the vocabulary size, every row's ids and labels, the padded batch with ids, labels, and masks, the trained count, the rejected empty completion, and OK; python/fixtures/expected-output.txt holds that output byte for byte

python starter.py prints NOT OK and exits 1 as shipped; after the practice change example one drops two prompt tokens and example three one, the batch pads to 10, 20 of 30 real tokens train, and an eleven-token completion is rejected, as python/fixtures/expected-practice-output.txt records for practice_answer.py
constraints: Standard library only; each lesson file runs alone in an empty directory with python -I -S; no fixtures, credentials, tokenizer libraries, or network

ids and labels always have the same length; every prompt position and every pad carries -100; the completion and eos carry their own ids; the attention mask is 1 exactly on real tokens; the input examples are never modified
An empty completion raises ValueError naming the prompt; the practice rejects a completion that cannot fit the maximum length

Ordinary Python only: a dictionary as a growing vocabulary, list concatenation and repetition, slicing, max in a loop, tuples of parallel lists, sum over a mask, enumerate with zip, a percentage format; no classes, regular expressions, or comprehensions in the lesson files

Position by position, the labels ignore exactly the prompt and train exactly the completion and eos, pads never train, and the vocabulary assigns ids in order of first appearance with repeated words keeping theirs

starter.py run alone exits 1 with NOT OK and no traceback; practice_answer.py run alone exits 0 and matches expected-practice-output.txt, with the trained positions of every row preserved and the over-long completion rejected
What shipped is measured on the same batch: labels equal to the ids train 33 of 33 real tokens, 13 of them prompt, against 20 with the mask

visuals.description: A short animation of the worked example, three seconds per example and under half a minute in all: three rows of token boxes with the word above, the id inside, and the label below, grey where the label is -100, blue where the completion id is trained, green for eos; the pads appear hatched with ignore labels and a mask line of ones and zeros; the count totals 20 trained of 33 real tokens; a beat shows what shipped by turning every prompt label red and counting 33; the practice variation fades the dropped prompt boxes and slides the rows left to ten positions.
